userStories.title: Add rt analyze complexity command
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to run rt analyze complexity --solution X to get cyclomatic complexity, cognitive complexity, LOC, and parameter count per method across the solution, so that I can identify hotspots for refactoring.
acceptanceCriteria: ComplexityCommand class exists at src/RoslynTools/Commands/ComplexityCommand.cs as internal sealed class ComplexityCommand : IRtCommand
ComplexityCommand.Info.Name equals "complexity" and matches the first argument passed to new Command(...) in Build()
ComplexityCommand.Info.Category equals "analyze"
ComplexityCommand.Info.JsonOutput is true
ComplexityCommand.Info.Mutates is false
ComplexityCommand.Info.Examples contains at least one runnable invocation including rt analyze complexity --solution RoslynTools.slnx
Running rt analyze complexity --help prints help text describing --solution, --threshold, --sort, and --top flags
rt analyze complexity is reachable both as rt analyze complexity and as the unqualified rt complexity form, matching the existing convention enforced by App.RunAsync
dotnet build RoslynTools.slnx succeeds with zero errors after ComplexityCommand is added
dotnet format RoslynTools.slnx --verify-no-changes exits 0 after ComplexityCommand is added
dotnet test RoslynTools.slnx -v minimal passes with the new ComplexityCommand tests included
The startup registry assertion in App.cs does not throw when ComplexityCommand is reflection-discovered (Info.Category is one of the accepted values)
With a valid --solution path, command exits 0 and writes a single JSON document to stdout
With a valid --solution path, all progress and diagnostic messages are written to stderr, never stdout
Stdout JSON parses successfully via System.Text.Json.JsonDocument.Parse with no trailing or leading non-JSON text
JSON root object contains a methods array, a typeRollups array, and a namespaceRollups array

Each entry in methods contains exactly the keys method, type, namespace, file, line, cyclomatic, cognitive, loc, params with correct JSON types (string/string/string/string/number/number/number/number/number)
method field is the fully qualified method name including the containing type (e.g. RoslynTools.Core.WorkspaceLoader.OpenAsync)
type field is the fully qualified containing type name without the method portion
namespace field is the containing namespace string, or an empty string for types in the global namespace
file field is an absolute path to the source file containing the method declaration
line field is the 1-based line number of the method declaration opening in file
For an empty method void M() {}, cyclomatic equals 1 (base path)
For a method with a single if statement and no else, cyclomatic is 2 (base + 1 decision)
For a method with if / else if / else, each if and else if increments cyclomatic by 1; bare else does not add to cyclomatic
For a method with a switch containing N non-default case labels, cyclomatic increases by N over the base
for, foreach, while, and do-while loops each contribute +1 to cyclomatic
Each catch clause contributes +1 to cyclomatic
Each ternary (?:) operator contributes +1 to cyclomatic
Each ?? null-coalescing operator contributes +1 to cyclomatic
Each ?. null-conditional member access contributes +1 to cyclomatic
Each && and each || binary logical operator contributes +1 to cyclomatic
Each ??= null-coalescing assignment operator contributes +1 to cyclomatic
Non-default pattern switch expression arms each contribute +1 to cyclomatic; the default discard arm _ does not
cognitive for an empty method is 0
cognitive adds +1 per structural break (if, switch, loop, catch, ternary) at the outermost nesting level of the method body
cognitive applies a nesting multiplier: a structural break at nesting depth d adds 1 + d (e.g. an if directly inside a method body at depth 0 adds 1; the same if nested inside another if adds 2)
cognitive adds +1 for each else or else-if clause that interrupts linear flow
cognitive adds +1 for each transition between binary logical operator types in a sequence (e.g. a && b || c counts as 2: one && sequence and one || sequence), not +1 per individual operator
cognitive adds +1 for each direct recursive call to the enclosing method
loc counts only non-blank, non-comment physical lines inside the method body braces
loc for void M() {} is 0
loc for a method containing only return; on one line is 1
loc excludes lines consisting solely of // single-line comments
loc excludes lines that fall entirely inside a /* ... */ block comment and contain no executable tokens
loc excludes the opening and closing brace lines of the method body when those lines contain no tokens other than the brace
loc for an expression-bodied method int M() => 1; is 1
params equals the number of formal parameters declared on the method signature
params for static int M(this string s, int x) (an extension method) is 1, not counting the this parameter
params for a parameterless method is 0
Constructors are included in the methods array with method set to TypeFQN.ctor (or equivalent clear convention) and metrics computed as for regular methods
Property accessors get, set, and init are each included as separate entries with method names using a TypeFQN.PropertyName.get / .set / .init convention
Local functions declared inside a method body are reported as separate entries with method names scoped to their enclosing method
Lambda expressions and anonymous methods are NOT reported as separate entries; their complexity is folded into the enclosing named method or accessor
Abstract method declarations and partial method declarations without bodies produce no entry in methods
Auto-implemented properties with no explicit accessor body produce no entry in methods
Source files containing an <auto-generated> header comment are skipped entirely
Source files with a .g.cs or .Designer.cs suffix are skipped entirely
typeRollups entries contain type, namespace, methodCount, cyclomaticTotal, cognitiveTotal, locTotal, paramsTotal fields
typeRollups totals equal the sum of the corresponding per-method metric values for all methods of that type (across all methods, not just filtered ones)
namespaceRollups entries contain namespace, methodCount, cyclomaticTotal, cognitiveTotal, locTotal, paramsTotal fields
namespaceRollups totals equal the sum of the typeRollups values for all types in that namespace
With --threshold 0 (default), every analyzed method appears in the methods array
With --threshold 5, a method where every metric value is strictly less than 5 is excluded from the methods array
With --threshold 5, a method where cyclomatic equals exactly 5 is included (>= comparison, not >)
With --threshold 5, a method where cognitive is 7 but all other metrics are below 5 is included
--threshold does not affect typeRollups or namespaceRollups totals; rollups are always computed over all analyzed methods regardless of the threshold filter
--threshold -1 exits with code 1 and a descriptive stderr message stating the threshold must be >= 0; no JSON is written to stdout
--sort cyclomatic (the default) orders the methods array by cyclomatic descending; ties are broken by method name ascending
--sort cognitive orders the methods array by cognitive descending; ties are broken by method name ascending
--sort loc orders the methods array by loc descending; ties are broken by method name ascending
--sort params orders the methods array by params descending; ties are broken by method name ascending
--sort with an unrecognized value exits with code 1 and a stderr message listing the accepted values (cyclomatic, cognitive, loc, params); no JSON is written to stdout
--top 0 (default) does not truncate the methods array
--top 5 truncates the methods array to at most 5 entries after sorting is applied
--top N where N exceeds the total method count returns all methods without padding or error
--top -1 exits with code 1 and a descriptive stderr message; no JSON is written to stdout
--top truncation does not affect typeRollups or namespaceRollups; rollups still cover all methods
With no --solution flag and exactly one .sln or .slnx file in the current working directory, the command auto-detects it and proceeds successfully
With no --solution flag and no .sln or .slnx file in the current working directory, the command exits with code 1 and a stderr message indicating that no solution file was found
With no --solution flag and multiple .sln or .slnx files in the current working directory, the command exits with code 1 and a stderr message listing the candidate paths
--solution pointing to a path that does not exist exits with code 1 and a stderr error message; no unhandled exception propagates
--solution pointing to a file that exists but is not a valid solution exits with code 1 and a stderr error message; no unhandled exception propagates

Running rt analyze complexity --solution RoslynTools.slnx completes successfully, exits 0, and the JSON output includes at least one entry in methods referencing a method from the RoslynTools source (dogfood)
A solution that compiles but contains zero method declarations produces a JSON document with empty methods, typeRollups, and namespaceRollups arrays and exits 0
Async methods (async Task) are analyzed and the await expression does not add to cyclomatic or cognitive beyond the surrounding control structures
Iterator methods using yield return are analyzed and yield return / yield break do not add to cyclomatic or cognitive beyond surrounding control structures
--sort and --threshold and --top flags may all be combined in a single invocation and each behaves independently: threshold filters first, sorting is applied to filtered results, then top truncates
Tests are located under tests/RoslynTools.Tests/ in an Analyze subfolder (or the matching existing analyze test folder convention) and use with_<scenario>_<outcome> naming
Tests use a real .slnx fixture and do not mock the Roslyn workspace, compilation, or syntax tree APIs

Test suite includes cases for: empty method cyclomatic baseline, each decision branch type (if, switch case, for, foreach, while, do-while, catch, ternary, ??, ?., &&, ||, ??=, pattern switch arm), extension method param exclusion, threshold filtering (below, equal, above), each sort option, top truncation, auto-detect success / fail / ambiguous, missing solution path
After implementation, rt dump-help output lists analyze complexity with --threshold, --sort, --top, and --solution flags plus at least one example
rt analyze complexity --solution RoslynTools.slnx --top 10 exits 0 in under 60 seconds when run against the roslyn-tools solution
userStories.notes: New ComplexityCommand.cs in src/RoslynTools/Commands/. IRtCommand contract: Category=analyze, JsonOutput=true, Mutates=false. Metrics: cyclomatic (decision branches), cognitive (nesting-weighted), LOC (non-blank non-comment lines in body), params (excl. this for extensions). Flags: --threshold 0 (show all, >= filter), --sort cyclomatic|cognitive|loc|params, --top N. JSON output: methods[] + typeRollups[] + namespaceRollups[]. Rollups always cover all methods regardless of threshold/top. Solution auto-detection via existing pattern.
userStories.resolution: ComplexityAnalyzer service in RoslynTools.Core; ComplexityCommand (alias: cx) in RoslynTools.Cli/Commands. Metrics: cyclomatic, cognitive, LOC, params per method with type/namespace rollups. Flags: --threshold, --sort, --top. 37 tests all green.

userStories.title: Add --to-project flag to rt refactor move (cross-project file move, keep namespace)
userStories.description: As a developer using rt to enforce Clean Architecture, I want to run t refactor move --type X --to-project TourStore.Domain so that a .cs file physically moves to the target project's folder while keeping its existing namespace declaration unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: Running `rt refactor move --type TourStore.Domain.Models.Product --to-project TourStore.Domain --solution tour-store.sln` on a solution where Product.cs lives in TourStore.Api/Domain/Models/Catalog/ moves the file to TourStore.Domain/Catalog/Product.cs (preserving subfolder hierarchy) and leaves the `namespace TourStore.Domain.Models;` declaration unchanged.

When --to-project is provided WITHOUT --to-namespace, the handler does not rewrite the namespace token in the moved file and does not modify any using directives in any consumer .cs files across the solution.

When --to-project is provided WITHOUT --to-namespace and the source file lives in a subfolder, the destination path mirrors the relative subfolder under the target project root; behaviour is covered by an explicit test asserting the resulting absolute path.

When BOTH --to-project and --to-namespace are provided, the file is written to the target project's folder AND the namespace declaration is rewritten to the supplied --to-namespace value AND consumer using directives are updated solution-wide.
When --to-project references a project name that does not exist in the supplied --solution, the command exits non-zero with an error message containing the missing project name; no files are moved.
When --type refers to a type whose source file is NOT inside the source project's folder on disk, the command exits non-zero with a descriptive error and makes no filesystem changes.
When --to-project is the SAME project the type already lives in, the command exits zero (no-op) and reports `nothing to move` without touching any files.
Running with --dry-run alongside --to-project prints the planned source path, planned destination path, and any planned <Compile Include> removals but writes nothing to disk.
If the source project's .csproj contains an explicit `<Compile Include>` item for the file, the handler removes that item from the .csproj after a successful move.
If the source project's .csproj has NO explicit `<Compile Include>` for the file (modern SDK glob), the .csproj is left byte-identical post-move.
The --move-file flag is silently ignored when --to-project is set: passing `--move-file false --to-project TourStore.Domain` still moves the file.

RtCommandInfo for `refactor move` lists --to-project as an option with help text mentioning that --to-namespace becomes optional when --to-project is provided; verified by snapshot test against `rt refactor move --help` output.
MoveCommandHandler unit test covers: target project resolution via MSBuildWorkspace, file path computation, and .csproj <Compile Include> removal — each in a separate test method.
`dotnet build RoslynTools.slnx --nologo -v quiet` exits 0 with zero new warnings introduced by the change.
`dotnet test RoslynTools.Tests.csproj --nologo -v quiet` exits 0 with all new MoveCommandTests passing.
userStories.notes: Required by tour-store EP-007 (US-022, US-023). Target: MoveCommand.cs + MoveCommandHandler.cs + MoveCommandTests.cs in C:\code\roslyn-tools. --to-namespace becomes optional when --to-project is provided. Modern SDK projects auto-include by glob so no .csproj edits needed in typical case. Explicit <Compile Include> items must be removed when present.
userStories.resolution: Added --to-project flag to rt refactor move. Cross-project file moves with subfolder mirroring, optional namespace rewrite, explicit <Compile Include> cleanup, dry-run output, same-project no-op guard, and source-outside-project-dir validation. 15 new tests covering all ACs.

userStories.title: rt refactor add-dependency: mangles fallback constructors and parameter list formatting
userStories.description: Injecting into an existing service rewrites the fallback constructor instead of delegating it. Also emits poorly formatted constructor parameter lists.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a target class with a fallback constructor that delegates via `: this(...)` AND a full constructor that already has the dependency parameter and assignment, when `add-dependency` runs, the rewriter exits with status `AlreadyInjected` and reports no changes (Changed == false).

Given a class with a delegating fallback constructor (`: this(...)`) and a full constructor missing the dependency, when `add-dependency` runs, only the full (non-delegating) constructor receives the new parameter and field assignment; the fallback constructor is left textually unchanged.

Given a class with multiple chained delegating constructors (`: this(...)`) plus one terminal full constructor, the rewriter modifies only the terminal full constructor and leaves all delegating constructors untouched.
Existing behaviour preserved: a class with a single constructor that does NOT have `: this(...)` initializer still gets the parameter and assignment added (regression guard for non-delegating ctors).
Existing behaviour preserved: a class with no constructors at all still gets a fresh constructor synthesized (regression guard for the `needsNewConstructor` branch).

Given a constructor whose existing parameters are each on their own line (one-per-line formatting), when a new parameter is appended, the new parameter is emitted on its own line with leading trivia (newline + indent) matching the prior parameter.
Given a constructor whose existing parameters are all on a single line, when a new parameter is appended, the new parameter is separated from the previous one by a single space after the comma.
Given a constructor with zero existing parameters, when a new parameter is appended, it appears as `(NewType newParam)` with no stray leading space, newline, or comma.

Dogfood: `rt refactor add-dependency --type AddDependencyService --dependency ISolutionChangeWriter --solution RoslynTools.slnx --dry-run` reports the dependency is already injected with no diff emitted and exit code 0.
Build gate: `dotnet build RoslynTools.slnx` succeeds with no new warnings.
Format gate: `dotnet format RoslynTools.slnx --verify-no-changes` exits 0.
Test gate: `dotnet test tests/RoslynTools.Tests/RoslynTools.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~AddDependency"` exits 0 with all new and existing add-dependency tests passing.
userStories.notes: Repro: add-dependency --type AddDependencyService --dependency ISolutionChangeWriter --solution RoslynTools.slnx --dry-run
userStories.resolution: DependencyInjector now skips constructors with this(...) initialisers, fixing AlreadyInjected detection for the delegating-ctor pattern and preventing fallback ctors from being modified. AddParameterAndAssignment derives leading trivia from the existing parameter list: newline+indent for multi-line, space for single-line. 8 new tests.

userStories.title: Convert solution-not-found crash to clean exit-1 error message
userStories.description: As a developer using rt, I want a missing solution file to produce a clear error message and exit 1, not an unhandled FileNotFoundException stack trace.
acceptanceCriteria: When the --solution path does not exist, rt prints a single error line to stderr (e.g. 'Error: solution not found: <path>') and exits 1 — no stack trace
The same clean exit-1 pattern applies to any FileNotFoundException thrown during solution loading
The UseExceptionHandler in App.cs (or equivalent top-level handler) catches FileNotFoundException and formats it as a user-facing error
Exit code is 1 (not 0, not unhandled crash code)
No stack trace or 'Unhandled exception:' prefix appears in output
userStories.notes: P1. WorkspaceLoader.cs:84 throws FileNotFoundException; it propagates unhandled through the System.CommandLine pipeline. Catch at the top-level UseExceptionHandler in App.cs (or at the throw site) and emit a single stderr line. No stack trace in normal output.
userStories.resolution: Added TryHandleUserErrorAsync helper in App.cs middleware that catches FileNotFoundException, emits 'solution not found: <path>' via RtLog.Error, sets exit code 1, and returns without rethrowing. WorkspaceLoader.ResolveSolutionPath now passes the offending path as FileNotFoundException.FileName so callers can format without parsing the message. Subprocess-level test in CliBootstrap.cs verifies exit 1 + clean stderr + no stack trace.

userStories.title: Catch common exception types in UseExceptionHandler and emit clean exit-1 messages
userStories.description: As a developer using rt, I want routine exceptions (bad file, bad JSON, not-found) to produce a single clean error line to stderr, not an unhandled exception stack trace.
acceptanceCriteria: UseExceptionHandler in App.cs catches FileNotFoundException, IOException, InvalidOperationException, JsonException, and YamlException and emits a single 'Error: <message>' line to stderr with exit code 1
No stack trace or 'Unhandled exception:' prefix appears for these exception types

userStories.title: Guard .First()/.Last() calls in SymbolLocator and MethodExtractor against empty sequences
userStories.description: As a developer using rt, I want empty-sequence edge cases to produce a clear error rather than an InvalidOperationException crash.
acceptanceCriteria: No .First() or .Last() call in SymbolLocator or MethodExtractor throws InvalidOperationException when the sequence is empty
Each call site uses FirstOrDefault with a null check, or validates the collection is non-empty before calling First/Last
When an expected symbol or statement is not found, the command emits a descriptive error to stderr and exits 1 rather than crashing
userStories.urgencyReason: Same crash class as US-042 — .First()/.Last() on potentially empty sequences in SymbolLocator (~4 sites) and MethodExtractor (~8 sites). Mechanical, one TDD batch.
userStories.notes: P2. SymbolLocator.cs lines ~49, 96, 135, 188 and MethodExtractor.cs lines ~57, 164, 168, 378, 501, 529-532 call .First()/.Last() on sequences that could be empty under certain inputs. Replace with FirstOrDefault + null check or add pre-call validation.
userStories.resolution: No-op: all 12 .First()/.Last() sites are invariant by construction. SymbolLocator: all four sites are g.First() after GroupBy — a group always has at least one element. MethodExtractor: all eight sites flow downstream of the selected.Count == 0 validation at line 350, which throws InvalidOperationException("No statements found in lines X-Y...") before any First()/Last() call. AC3 (descriptive error + exit 1 instead of crash) is now satisfied automatically via US-042 catching InvalidOperationException and emitting Error: + exit 1. Verified end-to-end: rt inspect find-refs --symbol DoesNotExistSymbolFoo and rt refactor extract-method --start-line 9000 --end-line 9001 both produce descriptive stderr lines and exit 1. No code change needed.

userStories.title: Suppress MSBuild workspace warnings by default; opt in with --show-workspace-warnings
userStories.description: As a developer using rt, I want MSBuild workspace warnings suppressed by default so that NuGet audit noise and compatibility warnings from the loaded solution don't pollute rt's output.
acceptanceCriteria: All MSBuild workspace warnings are suppressed from stderr by default when rt loads a solution
A --show-workspace-warnings flag (or equivalent) re-enables them for debugging
Genuine solution load errors that prevent rt from running still exit 1 with a clear message
The [workspace-warnings] block does not appear in normal output
userStories.urgencyReason: Daily noise: MSBuild workspace warnings block pollutes every command's stderr. Suppress by default; --show-workspace-warnings opt-in.
userStories.notes: P2. Affects WorkspaceLoader / MSBuildWorkspace diagnostic handling. Suppress all MSBuildWorkspace diagnostics by default; add --show-workspace-warnings global flag to restore them. Genuine load errors (exit 1) must still surface.
userStories.resolution: No-op: --show-workspace-warnings global flag already exists (App.cs RegisterGlobalOptions line 235-236) and is plumbed through RtContext.ShowWorkspaceWarnings. Verified end-to-end: rt inspect describe ProjectX.Service.Services.ServiceController --solution ProjectX.Libraries.sln produces zero stderr lines by default (AC1, AC4); passing --show-workspace-warnings emits 26 lines of NuGet audit / MSBuild warnings (AC2); US-042 ensures genuine solution-load errors still produce Error: + exit 1 (AC3). All four ACs satisfied by existing code.

userStories.title: Introduce Result<T,RtError> for routine user-error flows in core services
userStories.description: As a developer, I want routine "not found" / "bad input" cases in SymbolLocator, MethodExtractor, WorkspaceLoader to return a Result type (success or RtError) instead of throwing InvalidOperationException, so the global exception handler can produce clean exit-1 stderr lines for known user errors while still surfacing real bugs with full stack traces — without resorting to substring-matching exception messages.
acceptanceCriteria: Add Result<T, RtError> (or equivalent ADT) in src/RoslynTools/Core/. RtError is a record with a Kind enum (NotFound, InvalidInput, AmbiguousMatch, WorkspaceLoadFailure) plus message and optional context dictionary.

Convert SymbolLocator.FindSymbolAsync / FindSymbolByFqnAsync / FindTypeByFqnAsync / FindMethodBySpecAsync to return Result<ISymbol, RtError>; routine "not found" / ambiguous cases produce RtError, never throw.
Convert WorkspaceLoader.LoadAsync to return Result<(MSBuildWorkspace, Solution), RtError> for the no-projects-and-failure-diagnostic case; throw only for genuinely unexpected exceptions.

MethodExtractor: routine user-input rejections (no statements in range, multiple parent blocks, return statements in selection, --after + --before conflict) become RtError; AST-rewrite-produced-no-changes and similar internal-invariant violations remain exceptions.
Update every caller of the converted APIs to propagate or handle the Result; commands surface RtError via a single RtLog.Error + context.ExitCode = 1 helper.

Add a typed-only catch ladder in App.CaptureExceptionAsync for FileNotFoundException, DirectoryNotFoundException, ArgumentException, JsonException — these are routine OS/parse errors. No substring-matching of exception messages anywhere.
feedback.json still captures every exception with the full diagnostic payload from US-042; only the user-facing stderr shape changes.
Tests: SymbolLocator returns RtError.NotFound for unknown symbol; OutlineCommand returns exit 1 + single stderr line for missing file; build remains clean.
Documentation: add a short Result-types section to CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md so new commands follow the pattern.
userStories.urgencyReason: Architectural fix that supersedes US-042+US-044: Result<T, RtError> for routine errors. Story explicitly cites 2026-05-15 quality-first rule. Sequenced after US-042/044 ship so the bug-class diagnosis is validated by quick fixes first.
userStories.notes: Driven by quality-first rule (2026-05-15): refuses the substring-matching shortcut and instead models routine vs bug differences in the type system. Replaces the deferred classification half of US-042. Large change — touches ~10-15 throw sites and every caller — sequence carefully via /execute with TDD.
userStories.pauseQuestion: Commit to introducing Result<T, RtError> ADT across SymbolLocator/WorkspaceLoader/MethodExtractor and the App exception ladder in one batch, or sequence it incrementally (e.g. SymbolLocator first, then WorkspaceLoader, then MethodExtractor) across smaller stories?
userStories.pauseContext:
13-effort cross-cutting architectural change. Story prescribes specific types (Result<T, RtError> ADT, RtError record with Kind enum {NotFound, InvalidInput, AmbiguousMatch, WorkspaceLoadFailure}) and a typed catch ladder in App.CaptureExceptionAsync — architectural commitments warranting a human call before an autonomous run sprays them across the codebase.

Blast radius: 4 SymbolLocator methods (FindSymbolAsync, FindSymbolByFqnAsync, FindTypeByFqnAsync, FindMethodBySpecAsync), WorkspaceLoader.LoadAsync (tuple-returning Result), MethodExtractor user-input validations (no statements in range, multiple parent blocks, return statements in selection, --after + --before conflict), and every caller of those APIs across src/RoslynTools/Commands/ (~30+ sites). Also adds typed catches for FileNotFoundException, DirectoryNotFoundException, ArgumentException, JsonException in App.CaptureExceptionAsync.

Supersedes the substring-matching deferred half of US-042 (which currently does substring-matching in App.TryHandleUserErrorAsync). Open question whether US-042's handler stays alongside the typed ladder or is replaced wholesale.

Verified: no existing Result<T> or RtError types in src/RoslynTools/Core/ (grep returned no matches). Start sha 1b4118d already had the promotion commit on main; no working changes attempted.

userStories.title: rt analyze solid: ISP detector — flag fat interfaces and NotImplementedException members
userStories.description: As a developer, I want rt analyze solid --principle ISP to flag over-broad interfaces and implementing classes that throw on members they cannot fulfill.
acceptanceCriteria: rt analyze solid --principle ISP --solution <sln> exits 0 and emits JSON to stdout
Output has a top-level 'ISP' key with sub-arrays for 'FatInterfaces' and 'UnimplementedMembers'
Each FatInterface item includes: InterfaceName, FilePath, Line, MemberCount
Each UnimplementedMember item includes: TypeName, MemberName, InterfaceName, FilePath, Line
--min-members <N> (default 7) is configurable for the fat-interface threshold
Classes throwing NotImplementedException or NotSupportedException on implemented interface members are flagged under UnimplementedMembers
rt analyze solid --principle all includes ISP results
userStories.urgencyReason: EP-006 epic in flight — ISP detector follows the US-032 SRP template (SolidAnalyzer, SolidResult, mirrored tests). Lowest-risk SOLID addition.
userStories.notes: P2. Two sub-checks: (1) interfaces with member count above threshold; (2) classes implementing an interface but throwing NotImplementedException/NotSupportedException on one or more members. Output grouped under 'ISP' detector key.
userStories.resolution: Added rt analyze solid --principle ISP detector. SolidAnalyzer.AnalyzeIspAsync flags fat interfaces (declared members >= --min-members, default 7) and concrete classes whose direct interface-method/property/event implementations throw NotImplementedException or NotSupportedException. SolidCommand wires --min-members and accepts ISP, SRP, or all. SolidResult.ISP block contains FatInterfaces and UnimplementedMembers arrays. 23 new ISP tests + 1 dogfood-driven regression test (skip compiler-synthesized members like record-synthesized Equals).

userStories.title: rt analyze solid: DIP detector — flag concrete constructor params and inline new calls
userStories.description: As a developer, I want rt analyze solid --principle DIP to flag high-level classes that depend directly on concrete types rather than abstractions.
acceptanceCriteria: rt analyze solid --principle DIP --solution <sln> exits 0 and emits JSON to stdout
Output has a top-level 'DIP' key with sub-arrays for 'ConcreteConstructorParams' and 'InlineNewCalls'
Each ConcreteConstructorParam item includes: TypeName, ParamName, ConcreteType, FilePath, Line
Each InlineNewCall item includes: TypeName, MemberName, ConcreteType, FilePath, Line
Value types, record types, and Exception-derived types are excluded from InlineNewCalls
Classes named *Factory, *Builder, or *Provider are excluded from InlineNewCalls (they are expected to new things)
rt analyze solid --principle all includes DIP results
userStories.urgencyReason: EP-006 — DIP detector, same template as US-032/033.
userStories.notes: P2. Two sub-checks: (1) constructors accepting concrete class params (not interfaces/abstract); (2) non-factory class bodies calling new ConcreteType() where ConcreteType is not a value type, DTO, or exception. Output grouped under 'DIP' detector key.
userStories.resolution: Added rt analyze solid --principle DIP detector. SolidAnalyzer.AnalyzeDipAsync flags concrete-class constructor parameters (excluding BCL System.* types, records, abstract classes, interfaces, value types) and inline new ConcreteType() calls inside non-factory classes. Classes named *Factory/*Builder/*Provider are skipped. SolidResult.DIP block contains ConcreteConstructorParams and InlineNewCalls arrays. 25 new DIP tests + dogfood validation against RoslynTools.slnx.

userStories.title: rt analyze solid: OCP detector — flag switch/if chains branching on concrete types
userStories.description: As a developer, I want rt analyze solid --principle OCP to flag code that must be modified every time a new concrete type is added.
acceptanceCriteria: rt analyze solid --principle OCP --solution <sln> exits 0 and emits JSON to stdout
Output has a top-level 'OCP' key containing an array of violation items
Each item includes: TypeName, MemberName, FilePath, Line, BranchCount, ViolationType ('switch' or 'if-chain')
Flags switch expressions/statements matching on 'is ConcreteType' patterns
Flags if/else chains using 'is ConcreteType' or 'obj.GetType() == typeof(X)' with 2 or more concrete-type branches
--min-branches <N> (default 2) is configurable
rt analyze solid --principle all includes OCP results
userStories.notes: P2. Detects: (1) switch expressions/statements matching on 'is ConcreteType'; (2) if/else chains using 'is ConcreteType' or obj.GetType() == typeof(X) with 2+ branches. Output grouped under 'OCP' detector key.
userStories.resolution: Added rt analyze solid --principle OCP detector. SolidAnalyzer.AnalyzeOcpAsync flags switch expressions/statements with 2+ arms matching on concrete-type patterns (DeclarationPattern, TypePattern, ConstantPattern resolving to a type) and if/else chains using 'is ConcreteType' or 'GetType() == typeof(X)' for 2+ concrete-type branches. Interface patterns and value comparisons are not flagged. --min-branches (default 2) is configurable. SolidResult.OCP is a flat array of OcpViolationItem with ViolationType ('switch'|'if-chain') and BranchCount. 16 new OCP tests + dogfood validation.

userStories.title: rt analyze solid: LSP detector — flag overrides throwing or narrowing contracts

userStories.notes: P2. Two sub-checks: (1) override methods whose body throws NotImplementedException/NotSupportedException; (2) explicit interface implementations that throw on every code path. Output grouped under 'LSP' detector key.
